doc.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Studio work, Rudy Van Gelder and Freddie Hubbard
title: Recording La Mer with Bernstein and other orchestral dates
summary: Laws recalls recording La Mer with the New York Philharmonic under Bernstein and a Gluck solo with Columbia Masterworks.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Yeah. I remember recording. When I was with the New York Philharmonic, I recorded La Mer. I remember that, because Len Bernstein was the conductor of the orchestra.
I think I have a copy of that.

That was one of the first experiences I had, because we had come up as kids with a concept that these guys don’t make mistakes, errors, but they did more cutting and editing on that session than I had ever seen. I say, wow, these guys make mistakes like we do. That’s true. That’s the only recording I remember. I did some other things too. I did a thing with some guy who recorded me as well as Chick. He played – Chick did Für Elise and I did Gluck’s Orpheus. I did the solo part. That was with an orchestra. It was released on Columbia Masterworks. And then the other thing I told you about, with Leonard Bernstein. Those were the only two I can recall. I’m sure I did some more.
